scope: Reader thumbnail navigation, preview decode width and spread-index preparation in portrait and landscape

findings.observed_before: A cover-to-spread-80 change in a 201-page widget fixture mounted intermediate artwork including pages 27-34, 55-62, 79-86 and later intermediate pages. Its 240ms scroll traversed unneeded previews.
change: Jump to distant targets instead of scrolling through them; preserve nearby easing within 1.5 viewports.
Treat geometry changes as immediate alignment and cancel an obsolete scroll activity when a rapid return targets the current position.
Apply the same distance/layout rule to the landscape rail.
Supply known item extents so distant positioning does not depend on incomplete extent estimates.

findings.observed_before: The visible cover photo provider was an unresized AssetImage. Both reader navigators used builders without previewImageDecodeWidth, allowing thumbnail photos to decode at original dimensions.
change: Use display-size/device-density thumbnail widths bucketed by 64, normally 128-512 pixels. Preserve an explicitly smaller incoming preview budget.
Use separate thumbnail builders for cover and interiors without mutating the supplied full-reader builder.
Keep full-page, zoom, print and turn-texture sizing functions unchanged. No new cache or pixel history is introduced.

findings.code_evidence: The landscape _spreadItems getter built every cover/interior pair and was called for itemCount and again for each built row. The horizontal strip also rebuilt the complete pair list on each widget rebuild.
change: Calculate spread count and visible row indices arithmetically. Only the current item pair is allocated during lazy row construction.
Retain the public spreads() helper behavior for existing callers; validate counts, cover grouping, odd endings, invalid indices and a billion-page arithmetic lookup in unit tests.
findings.measurement_limit: This is a code-supported removal of repeated grouping allocations, not a physical-device timing or allocator benchmark.

checked: Nearby movement still contains intermediate animation frames; distant movement immediately reveals the selected preview without intermediate page artwork.
Rapid return stops the earlier animation; both reduced-motion preferences remain immediate.
Cover and interior photo providers use bounded widths while the original full-size builder is unchanged; a caller-supplied 64px budget is preserved.
Actual portrait/landscape reader navigators handle a far focus update while optional turn textures are still preparing.
Count/index arithmetic retains every old cover/pair/final-page mapping and range error behavior.
Existing home cover geometry, book depth, photo recovery, fast selection, rotation, hidden/resume, memory pressure, tracked handles and pending/live image-cache cleanup regressions pass.
The existing per-build cover interaction behavior is preserved; no persistent interaction-map history or extra subscription was added.
Saved layers, z order, source photo references, titles, gallery/full-reader typography, catalog prices/ownership and store request/category behavior were not edited.
review.shared_workspace: No other task changes were reverted. Snapshots preceded these edits. Only the listed reader source/test files and this new verification record were written for this run.

initial_related_suite.failure_kind: Only the two new integration fixtures waited for an inner BookFlip widget before the optional atlas was ready. The reader and live thumbnail controls were already present.

integration_fixture_follow_up.change: Use the supported 80-page reader and drive its actual public focus callback while textures prepare; do not gate thumbnail interaction on atlas readiness. The standalone 201-page bound remains.

resource_incident.status: Final tests completed, but host storage remains low and needs attention before further compilation.
resource_incident.evidence: An earlier related-suite attempt failed before executing tests when Flutter could not copy output.dill: OS errno 28, No space left on device.
handling: Stopped/paused only this heartbeat-owned work when avoiding overlap with externally initiated profile QA. Did not terminate another task or the user device run.
Inspected only the known heartbeat compiler temp paths; Flutter had already removed them. No user files, shared build cache, global SDK cache or customer data were manually deleted.
Observed approximately 15 GiB free after compilation ended, then reran with --no-test-assets to reuse the valid asset bundle from the successful controlled tests.
Each agent-owned test invocation used concurrency=1; external profile QA restarted independently during portions of this run, so global exclusivity across other tasks is not claimed.
resource_incident.classification: Host storage/tooling interruption, not an app test assertion failure or a measured app memory leak.
resource_incident.cause_of_host_storage_and_swap_pressure: Not attributed to the app or one specific task; system measurements cover all current processes.

next_candidates: Before the next compiler/test run, recheck free disk and other active test processes. With less than 2 GiB free, prefer read-only review and record the environment limit; do not repeatedly compile or delete user/shared caches.
Review PageController replacement lifecycle in BookPageView and AlbumReaderSinglePageView; init/dispose listener ownership deserves a controlled replacement case before editing.
Continue reader/home async owner and cache recovery checks using recent verification records; do not repeat the completed store like/read changes without new evidence.
Coordinate test resource use with other active tasks if compiler storage failures recur.

limits: No physical-device frame time, peak process memory or visual quality profile was run. Width caps and skipped intermediate construction are verified widget/code properties, not measured FPS or MB savings.
Thumbnail decode widths are bounded; this is not an absolute byte budget for every unusual source aspect ratio. Existing global cache policies still apply.
An already-started shared image/atlas operation may finish after hiding. Existing activity/disposal gates remain responsible for stopping new work and discarding obsolete results.
The optional full-book atlas can still be preparing when the navigator is usable. The integration fixture deliberately verifies navigation before that optional renderer is ready.
